thread:
Claire Park: quick heads-up — Aurora's finance reached out about Q3 dedicated commits. they saw a huge spike in prod inference last month and want to revisit their buffer/burst terms.

Omar Diaz: what numbers are we looking at?

Claire Park: current committed is 10,000 GPU-hours/mo on p4 equivalence. observed usage in June averaged 12.5k but spiked to ~18k for a 10-day window (mostly daytime traffic). sustained baseline looks more like 11–13k.

Jen Liu: so peak >> commit. were they using burst credits or falling back to hosted?

Claire Park: they were on Dedicated, so we auto-bursted from pool for the spike. billing shows ~8k of burst above commit that month (+40%). Aurora is worried about cost predictability.

Ravi Patel: quick calc: if we set commit to cover 95th percentile monthly usage, that'd be around 15k GPU-hrs. if we offer a 20% buffer on top for predictable spikes -> 18k commit.

Jen Liu: 18k matches their worst week, but pushes them into a higher reserved tier price. would they accept higher commit at a discount vs pay-as-you-go bursts?

Pat (AE): pinging in — Aurora wants predictable invoicing, not surprise spikes. they'd consider increasing commit if we provide a soft cap/burst discount and a one-time onboarding credit. also they asked about regional constraints — most of spike was in us-west.

Omar Diaz: region note is important — our us-west pool was at 88% that week; we routed some jobs to us-east which increased tail latency. if we commit 18k we need to reserve capacity in us-west or guarantee cross-region fallback with latency SLOs.

Claire Park: propose 2 options to present to Aurora: 
• Option A: commit -> 15k GPU-hrs/mo (covers 95th pct), 15% buffer for burst (so we allow bursts up to 17.25k) at +10% over base rate. 
• Option B: commit -> 18k GPU-hrs/mo (higher commit), 25% discount on overage up to 2k hours, dedicated reserve in us-west with a small premium.

Jen Liu: can we model cost parity for them? if their current bill was commit+8k bursts, what does Option A vs B look like?

Ravi Patel: I ran a back-of-envelope with last month's numbers:
```
current: commit 10k @ $X -> $100k, bursts 8k @ $Y -> $48k, total ~ $148k
option A: commit 15k (@$X discounted 5%) -> $142.5k, expected bursts 2k @ burst rate -> $12k, total ~ $154.5k
option B: commit 18k (@$X discounted 12%) -> $158.4k, overage cushion used 0-2k @ reduced overage -> ~$0-10k, total ~ $158-168k
```
Numbers are illustrative — need exact rate sheet.

Claire Park: thanks Ravi. Ajdusting for real prices will matter. the tradeoff: Option A cheaper in month of big spike (surprised), Option B gives them predictable SLA and capacity in-region.

Pat (AE): Aurora cares about predictability and in-region capacity more than small monthly delta. they'd prefer Option B if we can include a 2-month free trial of the higher commit, and a commitment to reserve N GPU nodes in us-west during business hours.

Omar Diaz: reserving nodes during business hours is doable but we need to quantify what 'N' is. if they want 18k GPU-hrs/mo and 22 usable working days, that's ~818 GPU-hrs/day -> ~34 GPU-hrs/hour (~2–3 GPUs depending on instance size). but all depends on instance sizing.

Jen Liu: also remind that continuous batching and KV cache reduces token cost; if they adopt prefix caching they may lower sustained hours by ~10%. worth proposing an Optimize review as part of the package.

Claire Park: action items:
• @Ravi — update the pricing calc with actual X/Y rates and produce a 6-month forecast (incl seasonal: Q4 expected +25%).
• @Omar — check us-west pool headroom and what reserving 3-4 instance equivalents looks like for Q3 (capacity ops impact).
• @Jen — prepare Optimize review checklist and estimate potential hour reduction from caching/quant.
• @Pat — coordinate with Aurora for a decision meeting next week; offer the 2-month trial conditional on signed MSA.

forecast-bot: new forecast uploaded: https://redwoodinternal/forecasts/aurora-q3-v2 (chart + table).

Ravi Patel: on the 6-months forecast I'll include seasonal adjustments: historically their product ramps 15–25% in Sept–Nov. will simulate both a conservative +15% and aggressive +30% scenario.

Omar Diaz: note about networking: if we pin capacity in us-west we should set up private peering verification with Aurora — their egress patterns during spike saturated a transit link. need network team sign-off.

Jen Liu: if they accept Optimize review we can probably shave 1.2–1.6k GPU-hrs/mo via batching and quantization on their top 3 pipelines. that makes Option A more attractive.

Claire Park: good point. leaning toward offering a hybrid: start with Option B reserved in-region for first 2 months (trial), run Optimize -> if we can reduce sustained hours to <=15k, then convert to Option A pricing at renewal. keep burst buffer policy: bursts up to 10% free, then tiered overage.

Pat (AE): that hybrid sounds like the exact ask they made last call. I'll draft term language and run it by legal.

Claire Park: ok — I'll summarize and send to Aurora + include the forecast link. meeting scheduled Tue 10am PT. thanks all. :thumbsup:
